verdict.rationale: The GitHub repo is still public and free to fork and build under its license, but only "as is and without support or warranty" (daytona-gh-1). Community discussion notes Daytona has gone closed source (daytona-comm-6), which suggests the public code may not match the current hosted product. A user did compile and run an earlier version themselves (daytona-comm-3), so self-hosting is possible only through an unsupported, possibly stale codebase. Missing for 10: first-party self-hosting or deployment documentation, an actively maintained open-source core matching the current product, and vendor support for self-hosted installs.
